01 — Visual north star

What this brand must feel like

The brand should feel like: A late-night bar visit in a Vietnamese neighborhood. Warm pendant lights, the sound of the bar filling up, your crew already in a booth. The kind of place you tell people about on Sunday.

Not like: A family restaurant chain, a fast-casual rice bowl spot, or a clean minimal food-delivery page. Not polished for a corporate lunch. Not designed for strangers.

One-line visual thesis

Street-born Vietnamese energy — warm, moody, and built for a night out.

02 — Direction mix

Editorial / Human leads

Editorial / Human — 70% Cutting-edge / Innovative — 30%

The Editorial / Human direction gives this brand its warmth: photography breathes, copy sounds like an invitation, and nothing is engineered for conversion. The 30% Cutting-edge / Innovative layer sharpens it — confident type hierarchy, purposeful spacing, and a component system that signals a brand with intent. Equal balance between the two would strip the warmth without adding the editorial depth it needs.

What this mix prevents

  • A generic food-delivery brand feel: red buttons on white, badge copy, delivery-first hierarchy
  • Cold typographic minimalism that reads as design for its own sake
  • Over-produced lifestyle photography that loses the candid bar energy
  • SaaS-adjacent UI patterns that make a restaurant look like a software product
    03 — Color system

    Dark base. Gold anchor. One red accent.

    Near-black and warm brown neutrals hold 65% of every page; they are the atmosphere, not the backdrop. Gold carries all interaction and brand emphasis at 20%. Crimson appears once, in the bar promo strip only.

      • 04 — Typography system

      Be Vietnam Pro leads. Cormorant Garamond accents.

      Be Vietnam Pro runs 90% of the page: body copy, navigation, labels, buttons, and all short-sentence headline copy. It stays clear and direct on dark backgrounds at every weight. Cormorant Garamond enters at 10% for hero taglines and featured pull quotes; its editorial warmth signals presence where utility would flatten the moment.

      05 — Layout rhythm

      Flow-based narrative scroll

      The page moves like a night out: atmosphere first, then food, then the reason to stay. It must not feel like a restaurant ordering app or a modular content dashboard.

      Section banding sequence

      Saturday karaoke section
      --color-surface (#241810)
      CTA band

      Section patterns used

    • Full-width narrative band (hero, atmosphere) — no max-width constraint on the background; content max-width: 1200px centered

    • Proof band — featured 5-star review at large scale with Cormorant Garamond gold quote mark; credential bar below
    • Bar promo strip — full-width crimson section, gold text, gold CTA; this is the page's single red moment
    • CTA band — full-width, centered, gold primary button; appears above the footer

        07 — Proof presentation

        Trust through specificity

        Quán Phở carries a medium trust burden: the brand incorporated in March 2025, Yelp volume is still low at 9 reviews, and food quality shows some polarization in early feedback. The proof strategy front-loads everything verifiable — Google stars, the bar and cocktails, the karaoke night, the Long's Noodle House lineage — and defers booking and delivery claims until the client confirms those flows.

        Phase 1 — Launch proof (available now)
        • 3 × 5-star Google reviews on the homepage
        • Yelp 4.0★ with review count displayed
        • Business lineage: "Formerly Long's Noodle House — same family, same address"
        • Bar promo: "1 free spring roll with any bar drink. Sit at the bar."
        • Saturday karaoke callout: "Every Saturday at 8PM"
        • 13 professional food photos + 3 moody interior shots
        Phase 2 — Deferred until client confirms
        • Party booking CTA — no confirmed capacity or process
        • Delivery copy — no confirmed platform or service zone
        • Price range display — no confirmed pricing tier
        • Founder story — not yet verified
        • Review volume milestones as Yelp/Google ratings grow

        What must never be fabricated

      • Do not invent party capacity, deposit amounts, or booking process details
      • Do not display a delivery CTA until the platform and service zone are confirmed by the client
      • Do not add a price range or value framing until the client confirms the pricing tier
      • Do not write a founder story until the client provides verified details
      • Do not claim awards, press mentions, or year-established credentials without sourced evidence
          • 08 — Imagery and art direction

          Show the bar. Show the food. Show the energy.

          Photography direction

          Atmosphere / Interior3 existing moody interior shots — pendant lights, bar area, Vietnamese street mural, bougainvillea vinesUse for hero and full-bleed sections; dark-dominant; no brightness correctionFood close-up13 professional photos — close-up, high-contrast on white plates and wooden boardsUse in menu card grid; preserve original framing and contrast; no cropping that removes contextBar / cocktailSpicy Pho Ti-Ni and bar counter; warm evening ambient lightUse in bar promo section and karaoke callout; angle should show the bar social contextPeople / group energyGroup shots at the bar; candid-to-documentary style neededUse in social-proof and karaoke sections; shows the crowd, not a solo diner

          Never use these

        • Stock photography of any kind — the existing library is the only asset
        • White or bright backgrounds in hero or atmosphere sections
        • Studio-lit clean food photography that contradicts the moody dark interior look
        • Solo portrait shots of a single diner — the brand is group and bar energy
        • Parallax scrolling effects on the hero image
        • Low-resolution screenshots of Google Maps or review cards used as imagery
        • Illustrations, icons, or food emoji anywhere in the page layout
            • 09 — Motion and interaction

            Restrained. Purposeful. Never decorative.

            Motion rules

            Scroll revealFade-up — sections enter from 12px below at opacity 0300ms easeAll page sections; must respect prefers-reduced-motion; not staggered between cardsButton hoverGold (#F2B928) background dims to #E0A820150ms easePrimary and secondary buttons only; no scale transform, no glow, no rippleLink / nav hoverOpacity 1 → 0.75 on text links and nav items150ms easeNavigation and inline text links

            What must never animate

          • Hero image — no parallax, no Ken Burns zoom, no scroll-triggered scale transform
          • Button hover — no scale, no box-shadow glow, no ripple or ink effect
          • Text — no typewriter effects, no character-by-character reveals, no word-by-word transitions
          • Background — no gradient color cycling, no animated noise or texture overlays
          • Cards — no staggered entrance; the group reveals together, not one by one
          • Auto-playing video loops in the hero — not supported; use still photography

              • Easing curves

              --ease: cubic-bezier(.32,.72,0,1) — UI transitions

              --ease-soft: cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) — scroll reveals

              11 — Do / Don't rules

              Blunt. Visual. Operational.

              Do

              • Use existing dark moody interior photography as the visual anchor for every atmospheric section
              • Name the cocktail and dishes specifically in callouts — "Spicy Pho Ti-Ni," not "signature cocktail"
              • Put the gold CTA button above the fold on every major section
              • Show both CTAs (Order Now + Book a Party) in the hero — both are live
              • Use Be Vietnam Pro Bold for all short-sentence copy
              • Keep the bar promo strip (free spring roll) visible early in the page flow
              • Signal Saturday karaoke night with its own dedicated section or callout
              • Use warm gold `#F2B928` for all interactive emphasis — one accent color, consistently applied
              • Allow photography to breathe — generous padding on the dark base
              • Use "formerly Long's Noodle House" lineage as trust copy

              Don't

              • Don't use red as the dominant color on any page — crimson belongs to accent and bar promo strip only
              • Don't add delivery copy until confirmed by client
              • Don't use any stock photography — the existing photo library is the asset
              • Don't use a light or white background on any full-page section
              • Don't introduce a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete system
              • Don't use emojis, fire icons, or "hot items" callouts in the UI
              • Don't use the neon green `#52E074` outside the logo mark
              • Don't use "authentic" as a standalone descriptor — replace with the specific dish or tradition
              • Don't apply parallax effects to the hero image
              • Don't add language switcher without confirmed bilingual content need

              13 — Implementation notes

              What must be preserved. What can flex.

              Must preserve exactly

            • Cormorant Garamond Italic in gold (#F2B928) for the hero tagline — the signature display moment; never substitute or reweight
            • Bar promo strip in crimson (#C23528) — appears once, above the footer; this is the page's only red-dominant section
            • Both CTAs (Order Now + Book a Party) above the fold in the hero; neither can be deprioritized or hidden behind a scroll
            • Be Vietnam Pro Bold uppercase for all button labels — font family, weight, and case are locked
            • Neon green (#52E074) restricted to the logo mark only; never appears in the page layout
            • No light or white background sections — every section uses --color-base or --color-surface
            • Card border: 1px solid rgba(92, 66, 50, 0.4) on dark base; no drop shadows

                • Accessibility

              • All text on dark backgrounds must meet WCAG AA contrast: gold (#F2B928) on near-black (#181008) passes; verify cream (#F0E8D0) body text as well
              • All scroll-reveal animations must honor prefers-reduced-motion — remove the 12px offset and opacity transition when motion is reduced
              • Interactive elements (buttons, nav links) must have visible focus states — gold outline or ring on keyboard focus; never remove :focus-visible
              • Images must carry descriptive alt text, e.g. "Interior of Quán Phở bar with warm pendant lights and Vietnamese street mural" — not "restaurant photo"
              • Primary button contrast: dark (#181008) on gold (#F2B928) passes WCAG AA; gold text on dark base also passes
              • Body copy must stay at 16px minimum; 12px kicker and caption sizes must not carry critical information
              • The MealKeyway order link must open in a new tab with an aria-label that names the destination and behavior

                  • Future agents must never improvise

                • Do not add a third typeface — Be Vietnam Pro + Cormorant Garamond is the complete and locked system
                • Do not write delivery, party booking, or price range copy until the client confirms those details
                • Do not use crimson (#C23528) outside the bar promo strip; it is not a primary brand color
                • Do not add illustrations, icons, emoji, or food badge graphics — the brand is photo-only
                • Do not apply a light or white background to any full-page section
